coordinator_cost.verdict: The reference-patch rule is cheap and it pays for itself twice over, but not the way it was sold. Writing three throwaway solutions cost about 8.5 minutes and 12 frontier turns -- against a worker spend of $0.13 for one usable implementation, that is not obviously a saving. Its real value was diagnostic: the M-2 patch is what surfaced that L-4 supersedes three shipped fixtures, before a single worker token was spent, and the M-5 patch is what caught an anchoring rule that would have broken an assertion the shipped T-3 oracle already made. Both would otherwise have been discovered as a red gate at $0.09 a look.

findings: The class is on. M-5, M-8, M-6a and M-6b all went green on the first attempt, on one outcome, one writable file and one attainable red oracle each, for between $0.011 and $0.040 a packet.

Rule 9 held on every packet that tested it. The only packet that ever failed on the model's side, V5-M2, was the only restructuring one; every additive packet since has gone green first attempt. V5-M2's attempt 1 is still the clearest evidence: the worker emitted 131072 output tokens without producing a single tool call and was truncated before any write landed.

The reference patch did not buy correctness. Two packets frozen without one both went green first attempt and were the cheapest runs of the session. What a reference patch bought, twice, was catching a bad packet before dispatch -- and on M-6a the L-2b read trace caught exactly that class of defect for free.

Hand-pass item A is the highest-leverage line changed all session. Before it, oracle_reads_within_paths was unobtainable for every Python oracle in the repository, because openat's directory-fd argument was being resolved against the checkout. After it, three packets validated with all three of rule 2's fields true -- and on M-6a the restored check immediately rejected an over-broad oracle that would otherwise have been dispatched.

The loop still cannot finish. remote-add and push work; pr-create dies on GitHub's 65536-character body limit, and the branch it pushes points at starting_commit because the driver never commits the worker's changes. Two additive fixes in an unprotected file stand between here and an unattended PR.
M-1's gate-red-twice stop fired in production on the second packet it ever saw, on exactly the evidence it was designed to read, and refused the hand-off. The L-2 stop conditions work.

Six shipped fixtures were superseded across the session -- three by L-4, two by M-8, one helper by M-8's git calls. Each carries a comment naming what superseded it. A row that changes what an earlier row pinned is normal in a sequenced track; the discipline that made it safe was giving every supersession to a fresh author rather than editing the oracle to fit the implementation.
L-1b is done as-is: the opencode export path is removed rather than repaired, and the worker transcript survives in the run receipt's worker.stdout beside the receipt. It is no longer a debt line.

findings.summary: A packet's gate runs only that packet's oracle, so a diff can pass its gate and still break a contract the oracle never exercises. M-9's positional PR_STEP_NAMES indexing did exactly that; the §4.6 merge-preview caught it.
findings.open_question: whether a packet should carry a second, broader command as a non-starts_red guard wherever one is green at the starting commit. M-6a did exactly that and it cost nothing.

findings.summary: Rule 9 bounds additive-vs-restructuring but not how much is added. Both packets were additive and single-file, and both finished with finish_reason: length at 131072 output tokens having emitted no tool call. M-10 added four things at once.
findings.proposed: bound a mechanical_bulk packet by the number of independent additions as well as by their kind; the oracle's own class partition is a usable seam.

findings.summary: A frozen oracle was proven red at starting_commit and never proven green anywhere. It contained a fixture no correct implementation could pass, and the packet still validated fit: prepare's registered-commands-green-cold and acceptance-properties-discriminating both check redness, not attainability. The worker spent 1 509 082 tokens against a 1 000 000 ceiling chasing it.
findings.cost: $0.149579 and one wasted dispatch, plus the re-freeze
findings.why_it_got_through: rule 2 made oracle.reference_patch SHOULD at Amendment 2, and rules 9-11 tightened the packet's shape without ever requiring the oracle be shown green against a known-good implementation. Cutting an inherited oracle into three, as the M-10 split did, is exactly the operation that can introduce this and exactly the case where no reference patch existed.
findings.proposed: for any packet whose oracle was cut, inherited or otherwise not written fresh against a known-good implementation, require proof of green in both directions before dispatch. It does not need a throwaway solution: running the oracle against a rejected attempt's own diff found this in one command, and for a fresh oracle a reference patch already reports oracle_attainable.
findings.related: rule-11-narrowed-the-gate -- both are the same shape: the gate measures less than the reader assumes it does.

findings.summary: Every packet since V5-M9 carried the same limits block: soft 500000, hard 1000000. Observed spend ranges from 206 566 tokens (M-10a) to 1 509 082 (M-10c attempt 1) -- and varies by nearly 3x between runs of one unchanged packet. A single constant is inside that variance band, so it stops runs that would have succeeded, at random.
findings.note: the ceiling did its job as written; the fault is that the number was copied from packet to packet rather than set for each. Cost never came close to binding: $0.15 against $3.00.
findings.proposed: Treat a hard token stop as a soft outcome when the cost cap is untouched: let gate run on the work already produced rather than discarding it. Two of M-10c's three runs produced correct diffs that were thrown away while cost stood at $0.15 against a $3.00 cap. Setting limits per packet from fixture count does NOT solve this, because the variance is run-to-run.
findings.correction: an earlier reading of attempt 1 attributed its token burn to the oracle defect. Attempt 2 on the fixed oracle spent 1 435 896 tokens, so the oracle defect was real but was not the cause of the burn. Both facts stand independently.
findings.correction_2: Attempt 3 falsifies this finding's central claim. It stated the ceiling 'sits below what the packet costs'; attempt 3 ran the same packet for 533 033 tokens, well under the original 1000000. Spend on an unchanged packet varied 1 509 082 / 1 435 896 / 533 033 -- a factor of nearly three. The ceiling did not sit below the packet's cost; it sat inside the packet's variance band, which is a different and more awkward problem: no single constant is safe, and calibrating per packet from fixture count would not have helped either, because the variation is between runs of the SAME packet.

findings.summary: M-9's oracle pinned PR_STEP_NAMES as an exact 4-tuple and its real-git proof asserted the commit's diff equals the gate's touched paths exactly. M-10c's spec row requires inserting receipt-capture at the head and requires the captured files to be in the commit. Both assertions therefore had to fail, and templates/dispatch/tests/** is protected, so no worker could reconcile them. M-10c's own gate was green; the merge-preview was red at 7.
findings.caught_by: the §4.6 merge-preview, for the second time. It has now caught more real defects than the gates have.
findings.classification: coordinator defect at freeze time. Freezing a packet that changes a shape a prior oracle pinned must carry the prior oracle's reconciliation.
findings.proposed: when freezing a packet whose spec changes a constant, a signature or a set that an existing oracle asserts, reconcile that oracle in the freeze commit. An exact-equality assertion on a shape later packets are specified to extend is the smell; assert the invariant the row actually owns instead.
findings.attestation_note: the relaxations were authored by the same session that dispatched M-10c, which is the one part of this packet with no independent attestation. Rule 4 names oracle design an owner touchpoint; PR #73 is deliberately left unmerged for that reason.

d8.caveat: D-8 asks for >=5 green first pass with 0 escalations. All five greens carry exactly one escalation each, always the same one: the driver's PR step. None is attributable to the worker -- every gate passed, containment held, and every run was qualification-eligible. Whether a harness escalation spends the D-8 budget is the owner's ruling.

The branch it pushed points at the packet's starting_commit: post_gates reads the diff from the working tree with git diff --name-only <starting_commit>, and nothing commits it between the worker finishing and the push. Even with a short enough body the PR would have been empty.

reference_patch_cost.verdict: Four reference patches cost about 9.9 minutes and 16 frontier turns. Their value was diagnostic rather than instructive: two of the four surfaced a defect before a worker token was spent (M-2's oracle supersession, M-5's over-tight anchoring rule), and none of the four was ever seen by the worker. Then the two packets frozen WITHOUT one -- the first ever -- both went green first attempt, at $0.0173 and $0.0112, the cheapest runs of the session. On additive packets the reference patch is not buying correctness. What it buys is early detection of a bad packet, and on M-6a the L-2b read trace bought that instead, for nothing. The honest reading: keep it optional, and let validate's own checks be the freeze-time gate.

debt_for_v5_9: The PR body must be a bounded summary; section 4.5's 'the receipt is the body' cannot hold against a 65536-character limit.
The driver must commit the worker's changes in the worktree before pushing.

dispatch_release._path_allowed is a weaker matcher than hybrid_dispatch._matches_any: directory-prefix patterns like 'docs/' match in the gate and not in the driver's stop condition. Latent while packets use '**' globs.
mechanical_bulk is both a hybrid route and an action class -- a naming debt since L-3.
The manifest schema is still not machine-enforced; validate_hybrid_dispatch holds the invariants by hand.
